newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tsingtao sales rise 18 pct in 1st qtr.
newsitem.headline: Tsingtao sales rise 18 pct in 1st qtr.

text.p: Tsingtao Brewery Co Ltd said on Friday that sales volume in the first quarter of 1997 rose 18 percent over the previous year and that it expected better profits in 1997 compared to last year.
Tsingtao posted a 3.5 percent increase in turnover to 1.43 billion yuan in 1996 from the previous year, while net profit dropped 73.7 percent to 25.68 million yuan.
The Chinese brewer said sales of its Gold Label beer was expected to double this year to 40,000 tonnes.
"Since the canned Gold Label Beer is scheduled to be launched in the market in June 1997, the compnay will then experience better profits," it said in a statement.
The company attributed the big profit drop in 1996 to the write off of 28 million yuan in obsolete inventories and a total 51 million yuan loss in three of its beer subsidiaries.
"In the coming year, the company will endeavor to minimize the loss of Factory Number Four, Yangzhou Brewery and Xian Co Ltd," Li Gui Rong, chairman of Tsingtao said in the statement.

Tsingtao, China's second largest beer producer, also said in 1997 it would focus on building up a direct sales and marketing management network, rationalising its product portfolio and increasing promotional fees to ensure a steady increase in market shares and strengthen its competitiveness in China.

The company planned to spend about 220 million yuan this year to upgrade a canned beer production line, the construction of an inspection and training centre and upgrade the technology at its Factory Number Four.

It also said the construction of Tsingtao Brewery (Shenzhen) Co Ltd commenced in March and production was expected to start at the end of 1998 with the first stage annual production capacity at 100,000 tonnes.
Tsingtao Brewery (Shenzhen) is a joint venture between the company and Pine Seal Development Ltd.
Shares of Tsingtao eased HK$0.20 to HK$3.35 at midday on Friday after the results announcement on Thursday.
